topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway

Egress IP allowlisting and NAT/Firewall constraints
POC success criteria: latency, throughput, accuracy
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-15 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC | Duration 45m
Attendees: Nina (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood SE), Aisha (Pharmalink), Tom (Pharmalink), Victor (Pharmalink), Sara (Pharmalink)

[00:00] Nina: hey everyone thanks for joining, can folks hear me ok?
[00:05] Aisha: yeah loud and clear, thanks Nina. we've got about 45 minutes, nice to meet you all.
[00:12] Marco: awesome, i'll kick off with a quick agenda — private networking options, residency constraints, sample workloads and success criteria, and then we can map next steps.
[00:20] Tom: perfect, our main ask is that data never leaves eu-west-1 and that connections are only over our approved egress IPs, plus we need audit trail details.
[00:28] Marco: understood. quick clarifier — for private networking we support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoints), and for larger setups transit gateway. each has tradeoffs on maintenance and cross-account routing.
[00:40] Sara: our security team prefers PrivateLink historically because it reduces blast radius and you don't expose route tables, but peering is simpler if low complexity. can you run us through the practical differences?
[00:50] Marco: sure — with VPC peering you create a peering connection between PharmaLink VPC and Redwood's service VPC. that requires route table updates and doesn't support transitive peering. PrivateLink instead exposes an interface endpoint in your VPC and traffic goes to our NLB, so you get private ENIs and you only need to allow the endpoint's IPs.
[01:05] Victor: do you publish specific IPs we need to allow? our firewall team wants explicit CIDR ranges.
[01:10] Leah: for hosted private we can provide a short list of egress IPs for allowlisting. for dedicated or private deployments inside customer infra, egress is within their own network. note: sometimes the autogenerated docs show NLB IP ranges which can change, we'll provide a stable list for the POC.
[01:24] Aisha: good. on residency — we need models and logs to remain in eu-west-1. can Redwood pin region for the POC and ensure telemetry isn't sent to us-east?
[01:32] Nina: yes we can pin to eu-west-1 for the POC. for hosted-private setups we host inference in that region and we can configure log retention to a region-specific S3 or to customer-managed logging if preferred.
[01:45] Tom: what about KMS — do you integrate with customer-managed KMS keys? we need key ownership.
[01:51] Marco: yes, for Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For hosted private we offer a customer-managed key option via cross-account KMS grants. we'll share the pattern in the security playbook.
[02:02] Sara: egress constraints — we have egress only via a set of NAT gateways and a firewall appliance. we can't allow arbitrary internet egress from the VPC used for models. will PrivateLink work in that topology?
[02:12] Leah: PrivateLink works fine behind NAT as long as the interface endpoint can communicate to our NLB — you just need to allow the endpoint to reach our service ports. we'll document required ports and healthcheck addresses.
[02:23] Victor: what ports are needed?
[02:26] Marco: typically HTTPS 443, and optional gRPC endpoints on 443 as well. No unusual ports. we'll give a minimal rule set.
[02:34] Aisha: switching into POC success criteria — our product team cares about latency (p95) for short-form generation, throughput for batch embeddings, and model quality parity with our existing on-prem endpoints. Typical target: p95 < 200ms at 50 concurrency for chat, embeddings throughput 200 req/s. is that feasible?
[02:50] Marco: it's doable with dedicated capacity and correct batching. for hosted-private with autoscaling you might see slightly higher tail latency under burst. we should baseline with your workload — what are typical sequence lengths and tokens per request?
[02:59] Victor: chat average 120 tokens output, input 40 tokens. embeddings are 768-d vectors, about 1-2 seconds per call on our current infra but we want to reduce cost and improve latency.
[03:12] Marco: ok that helps. for baseline benchmarking we'll simulate your average token distribution and target the 50 concurrency test to measure p95 and resource utilization. we usually run both single-request latency tests and sustained throughput tests (30+ minutes) to see autoscale behaviour.
[03:26] Nina: timeline-wise how fast do you want this POC?
[03:29] Aisha: we'd like a 2-4 week POC: week 0 network setup, week 1 baseline benchmarks, week 2 model adjustments + quantization experiment, week 3 decision/pilot. ideally 3 weeks.
[03:41] Marco: sounds reasonable. we can commit to a 3-week POC if we get the network details and a small sample data set to run benchmarks.
[03:49] Tom: about data handling — can you keep request logs masked? PHI might appear in prompts; we need redaction at rest and in transit plus a policy about storing prompts in logs.
[03:59] Leah: we offer configurable logging: no transcription storage for hosted-private, or redact sensitive fields using our SDK hooks. for Private (on-prem) logs remain in your cluster and never leave your control. we'll include the masking pattern in the checklist.
[04:12] Aisha: also need audit logs and SSO/SAML integration for RBAC.
[04:16] Nina: we support SAML SSO and RBAC; audit logs are part of our enterprise plan. we'll attach the SOC2 reports and our SSO integration doc.
[04:24] Victor: ok good. benchmarks — what tooling do you use? we've used locust and k6 previously.
[04:29] Marco: we typically provide a JMeter/k6 script plus a python load driver that hits the same endpoints as your SDK. we'll produce a playbook that includes warmup steps, KV cache priming, and batch size sweeps to find the latency/cost sweet spot.
[04:43] Tom: KV cache priming — will that skew results? we want production-like warm caches.
[04:48] Marco: we recommend running a warmup period that primes common prefixes and then measure. we'll run both cold and warm runs and share the delta.
[04:56] Aisha: on success criteria — let's capture specific numbers: p95 < 200ms for chat at 50 concurrent, embeddings average latency < 120ms at 100 rps, model quality parity with our baseline (BLEU and bespoke evals within 3% of current). if we hit those, we move to pilot.
[05:14] Nina: noted — we'll include those in the POC acceptance criteria.
[05:18] Sara: region again — eu-west-1 required for data residency, any backups or monitoring should be EU-only.
[05:25] Leah: yes we can configure metrics and logs to export to customer-managed endpoints in eu-west-1, or push to your S3 in the region.
[05:34] Victor: any dependency on US services for telemetry?
[05:37] Marco: not for the POC; we'll ensure control-plane interactions remain in eu-west-1 and avoid telemetry phone home to us-east. we'll confirm exact endpoints in the network doc.
[05:46] Aisha: what's the expected cost for the POC? we need a ballpark.
[05:50] Nina: for a 3-week POC with dedicated slice we usually estimate based on GPU hours used in the benchmark. rough ballpark — for the benchmark runs and a small dedicated pool, estimates usually range 8k-20k depending on model family and hours. we'll send a tailored estimate after we know model size and run duration.
[06:05] Tom: can you do a cost/per-token estimate using quantized models?
[06:09] Marco: yes we'll run quantization profiles and provide cost delta across int8/4-bit where supported. note that some models see slight quality regressions at aggressive quant; we'll surface those tradeoffs.
[06:20] Aisha: one more thing — legal/procurement loops. procurement wants an indemnity clause and data processing addendum. timeline for that might push pilot start, are you ok with that?
[06:29] Nina: yes that's normal. we'll share contract templates and DPA; legal reviews typically take 2-3 weeks but can overlap with network setup.
[06:36] Victor: to summarize next steps: Redwood sends security playbook, private networking guide and IP list; PharmaLink shares VPC cidr and approved egress IPs and compliance Qs; Redwood spins up benchmark playbook and schedule.
[06:49] Nina: exactly. Marco, can you confirm deliverables?
[06:52] Marco: i'll produce: 1) benchmark playbook + load scripts, 2) network doc outlining PrivateLink and peering steps and required ports/ips, 3) sample metrics dashboard template. target 2025-09-19 for docs and scripts.
[07:05] Aisha: sounds good. we'll aim to provide network details by 2025-09-18 and compliance items by 09-20.
[07:12] Tom: quick question — do you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes?
[07:18] Leah: yes — our rollout engine supports canary percentages, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to cheaper model variants or cached responses. we'll demo in the pilot if you want.
[07:27] Victor: that would be useful.
[07:29] Nina: okay any outstanding blockers?
[07:31] Sara: just internal calendar alignment, otherwise good.
[07:34] Marco: i'll note one caveat — if you want absolute single-digit ms p95 at high concurrency you likely need colocated dedicated hardware; for most web-app use cases we can meet the 200ms target with dedicated pools and batching.
[07:48] Aisha: understood. let's proceed.
[07:51] Nina: thanks everyone. i'll follow up with the security pack and the POC acceptance criteria doc.
[07:57] Tom: thanks all.
[08:00] [meeting end]

Notes on transcription: occasional partial words and name mis-hearings possible (e.g., KV cache heard as KV cash). Links referenced: security playbook (link: redwood.com/security-playbook.pdf), private networking guide (link: redwood.com/private-networking.pdf), benchmark repo (link: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-playbook)

POC Acceptance criteria (recap):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for chat at 50 concurrency
- Embeddings: avg latency < 120ms at 100 rps
- Quality: within 3% of baseline on evals
- Residency: all inference and logs in eu-west-1
- Security: SAML SSO + audit logs + KMS integration confirmed

Benchmarks planned:
- Cold start and warm cache runs
- Sustained 30-minute throughput tests
- Batching sweeps and quantization comparisons

Rough timeline:
- 2025-09-18: PharmaLink provides VPC CIDR and egress IPs
- 2025-09-19: Redwood delivers network doc + benchmark playbook
- 2025-09-22 to 2025-10-03: POC execution (3 weeks)
- Decision: by 2025-10-06
